facts.raw_span: a red tumor on her right upper arm that enlarged over 6 months
The lesion initially started as a small cutaneous nodule without obvious triggers
no history of local trauma or insect bite
a 6 × 6-cm protuberant, thick-walled, and well-defined red bullalike tumor on the right upper arm
a nontender, firm-to-hard nodule was palpated
no regional lymphadenopathy
Hematologic, biochemical, and urinalysis tests were normal
multilocular spaces below the epidermis and a solid tumor present in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface and lobulated appearance
basophilic cells and shadow cells in the deep dermis and dilated lymphatic vessels in the dermis above the tumor
results of the rest of the physical and systemic examinations were normal
extended 1 to 3 cm from the epidermal surface
her personal, past, and family histories were unremarkable

concepts.why: The presence of a well-defined, protuberant tumor with a chalky-white cut surface and lobulated appearance, along with basophilic cells and shadow cells in the deep dermis, is consistent with pilomatrixoma.
The initial presentation of a small cutaneous nodule that gradually enlarged into a firm-to-hard nodule is consistent with dermatofibroma.
The presence of a well-defined, protuberant tumor with a lobulated appearance and basophilic cells in the deep dermis is consistent with keratoacanthoma.
The initial presentation of a small cutaneous nodule that gradually enlarged into a firm-to-hard nodule is consistent with epidermal inclusion cyst.
The presence of a well-defined, protuberant tumor with a lobulated appearance is consistent with lipoma.
The initial presentation of a small cutaneous nodule that gradually enlarged into a firm-to-hard nodule is consistent with hemangioma.
The presence of a well-defined, protuberant tumor with a lobulated appearance is consistent with neurofibroma.
The initial presentation of a small cutaneous nodule that gradually enlarged into a firm-to-hard nodule is consistent with sebaceous adenoma.
